newsitem.title: USA: Fund manager sees global telecom mergers - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Fund manager sees global telecom mergers - Barron's.

text.p: There are a multitude of opportunities globally for telecom companies to combine and become more efficient, fund manager Oscar Castro told Barron's, the investor weekly newspaper.

Among a gamut of possible deals, he likes a complex British-oriented deal involving Bell Cablemedia Plc, an affiliate of BCE Inc ; Videotron Holdings Plc; and Cable and Wireless Plc, according to Barron's December 2 edition.

Cable and Wireless would merge its UK Mercury stake into NYNEX CableComms Group and the two other cable operators. The deal could create a stong player to compete with British Telecommunications Plc, Castro, who runs the Montgomery Global Communications Fund, said.
"We like the story and we need to decide how much we're willing to pay for it," he was quoted as saying.

But while Castro saw strategic advantages to the proposed merger between BT and MCI Communications Corp, he did not own stock in either company. Barron's said the manager did not like the "stand-alone" outlook for both companies.
Barron's said Castro felt Sprint Corp would likely remain out of play, with its fate decided by part owners Deutsche Telekom AG and state-owned France Telecom.
AT&T Corp would probably acquire or merge rather than be acquired, Barron's quoted Castro as saying.

Castro also said Vimpel-Communications, which provides cellular services in Moscow, was a "gift to investors," according to the newspaper, and he liked Venezuelan state phone company CANTV. Both investments were not without risks, he said.
